questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I'm studying German language and culture, so I wanted to study in a German city, where I could improve my language skills and get to know a new part of germany. Therefore was Frankfurt an ideal opportunity to follow.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: People were all so nice, and the academic personal have been so welcoming.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Got a lot of emails with all the information I needed.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Nothing, but the introduction-courses.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Nothing to complain about.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was actually pretty easy. I was searching for "WG's"/shared apartment to get to know some German people, and it was actually pretty easy to find.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's a good way to get integrated in the city. You meet some people, who are not exchange students, or students at the university. So you get a bit of a feeling of being a part of Frankfurt.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Compared to my hometown Copenhagen, was it pretty easy to find.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Easy, but not without problems

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I think that it was easy to make the registration for the university, but it was a bit confusing to find out how I could and which classes and courses, that I could follow. I needed to have som correspondences with the personal in Frankfurt to find out, so that part could have been a bit better.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I found the responsible professors on the homepage of Goethe-University in Frankfurt, and was in correspondence with these.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: After all the emails, it was as easy as it could be.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do it in advance and take your time to explore the website of the university.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very high level.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The academic level was the same as in Copenhagen, but since all my courses were in German, it was naturally a bit more challenging as it would be in Denmark.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Exactly the same.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Ringvorlesung "Liberté - Égalité - Europa. Frankfurter Frankreichforschungen" - Einzelansicht (2 ECTS) +
Lebensraum Europa 300-1600. Ein Überblick über die Neuordnungen der Geschichte Lateineuropas nach dem
Ende des Eurozentrismus - Einzelansicht (2ECTS)
Weltwirtschaftskrise und politische Krise: Das Ende der Weimarer Republik – Einzelansicht (4 ECTS)
Vor 100 Jahren - Die "Roaring Twenties": Kultur, Politik, Ökonomie – Einzelansicht (2 ECTS)
Kriegspropaganda. Die Frontberichte des NS-Rundfunks 1940-1945 (in Zusammenarbeit mit dem Deutschen
Rundfunkarchiv) – Einzelansicht (3 ECTS)
SPQR: Eine Sozial- und Institutionengeschichte der Römischen Republik – Einzelansicht (2 ECTS)

questions.answer: Publictransport. Cheap and effective with the Deutschlandsticket

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I spend a lot of time on "Hochschulesport", that means university sports. I was a part of the footballteam and a running club, and it gave a lot of fun.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Erasmus+ arranged a lot, and then common lunches in the Mensa.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The university-sports. It is really the best way to meet new people.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Use the "Deutschlandsticket" to travel around in the country and go to the footballmatches, museums etc.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy. I already spoke German, when I came her, so it was easy to settle in.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be openminded and ask them about everything. Don't take a no for an answer.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The German people can be a little bit introverted in their approach to people.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The politness, football and party ulture, the language

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be openminded, patient and don't be afraid to be nervous or to miss your hometown. You will quickly settle in to your new lifestyle and have a good time.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Try to prepare as much as possible in advance, so you are ready and openminded when you arrive.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The courses in German, and how it has helped me improving my language skills.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To make an one hour presentation in German for a class.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: It was a great success.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
